title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the collision. This shows a gap between what autonomous systems are trained to detect and respond to, and what they encounter in the world: the system's object recognition or collision avoidance did not treat a duck as an obstacle requiring evasive action.

Whether the system could have been caught before deployment depends on what testing covered. A human safety operator sat in the vehicle but did not intervene, which suggests either they did not detect the incident in time or the system's speed or trajectory was not identified as hazardous. The company has since excluded certain streets from its service area and is working on technological improvements through simulation, indicating the incident revealed a real-world failure in the system's current capabilities.

It is not established whether Avride's claim about the vehicle stopping at a stop sign reflects the actual sequence of events, since this remains disputed after the resident's account and the company's later data review.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping afterward. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant, and residents had grown attached to it. A neighborhood resident posted about the incident on Facebook, claiming the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this assertion after reviewing vehicle data.

In response to the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode at the time and has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. The company is evaluating technological improvements to prevent similar situations in the future through controlled simulations. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator. Avride continues testing on other public roads, and multiple autonomous vehicle companies operate in Austin.
